name: Wisconsin

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt; candy, soft drinks, dietary supplements and prepared food are taxed at the full rate, which is not counted here.

Cigarettes and other tobacco are taxed at the full rate, on top of excise taxes left out here: $2.52 a pack of cigarettes, 71% of the manufacturer's list price on other tobacco, and 5 cents a milliliter of vapor liquid.
Barber and beauty services aren't taxed.
Laundry, dry cleaning, pressing and dyeing are taxed; self-service coin-operated machines are not (since October 1, 2013).
Motor fuel is exempt from the sales tax and taxed by the gallon instead: 30.9 cents, unchanged since April 1, 2006, left out here.
Diapers and menstrual products are taxed at the full rate (2025 bills to exempt them stayed in committee, as reported).
Wisconsin has no sales tax holiday.

Hotel stays pay municipal room taxes (generally up to 8%; Madison 10%, Wisconsin Dells 5.5% plus its resort tax) and, in Milwaukee County, the Wisconsin Center District's room taxes, which are not counted here.
gaps: 6 cities lie in more than one county with a different rate in each county part; in each census tract such a city's rate is that of its part in the tract's county, counted for the share of the tract's store jobs located in the city.
1241 towns or townships that are not Census places have their rates listed here, matched to tracts through Census county subdivisions; all carry only the county rate.

Premier resort area taxes (10 places; 1.25% in Lake Delton and Wisconsin Dells, 0.5% in the others) and Milwaukee County's 0.5% food and beverage tax are administered outside the SST rate file; they are counted in the categories they fall on, as each place's notes say.

programs: Tax incremental districts are mapped from city and county layers; any the Department of Revenue lists as ended (its termination reports for 2023 to 2026, or a number below a municipality's highest active district that isn't on its April 2026 active list) is left out, since several maps still draw ended districts (Milwaukee's, Madison's, Adams', De Pere's and others). Madison's TID 55 (Voit Farm, 2025), Green Bay's newer districts (24 to 32) and Sun Prairie's TID 16 aren't on their maps. Business improvement districts are mapped for Milwaukee and Fond du Lac; Madison's Central BID and the Stevens Point and Sun Prairie districts have no official map. Enterprise zones are designated per company, and Main Street (36) and Connect Communities (94) have no map.
